# Plan: apt-mirror-worker

Make the snapshot-pinned apt mirror actually work by extracting it from `remote_service_connector` into its own project: a Cloudflare Worker serves the public routes straight from R2, and an operator-run CLI (no Modal at all) performs cut/warm/verify.

## Overview

- The mirror moves out of the connector entirely. The current placement is broken (the connector's `app.py` must be self-contained for `modal deploy`, and the `imbue.remote_service_connector.apt_mirror` import will `ModuleNotFoundError` in the deployed container) and wrong (public unauthenticated routes sharing a process with Cloudflare/Neon/SuperTokens/pool-SSH secrets; a global singleton jammed into per-tier deploy machinery; an `imbue-common`-from-PyPI dependency that would silently drift from the workspace version).

- Serving becomes a small TypeScript Cloudflare Worker at `apt.imbuepackages.com`, bound directly to the `apt-mirror` R2 bucket in the production Cloudflare account: dists objects are served frozen from R2, pool objects read through to the Debian upstreams on a miss, and pool responses are additionally cached at the Cloudflare edge. No Modal on the serve path: no cold starts, no egress cost, one less runtime between apt and the bytes.

- Cut/warm needs no service at all: with the Worker serving reads, admin operations are just "fetch from Debian upstreams, put to R2", so they run as an operator CLI (`uv run apt-mirror cut|warm|verify`) authenticated directly with R2 credentials from Vault. R2 write access *is* the authorization — no admin key, no admin routes, and registry write access stays as tightly held as the Vault entry.

- Warming is focused and finite instead of universe-scale: explicit committed package lists (starting with what dwt workspaces actually install), resolved against the cut Packages indexes for amd64+arm64, fetched in parallel, with read-through covering the long tail. `warm` exits nonzero on any unfetchable listed file; `verify` re-checks a cut without fetching.

- One global instance serves all tiers (no dev/staging/production), hosted in the existing production Cloudflare account since package-registry access must be tightly controlled. `apps/apt_mirror/current-timestamp` is the committed source of truth for the latest cut T; the dwt default apt source flips to `https://apt.imbuepackages.com` only after bring-up is verified.

## Expected behavior

- Workspaces and image builds resolve every apt operation against `https://apt.imbuepackages.com/snap/<T>/<archive>/...` by default: `write_apt_sources.sh` now defaults `APT_MIRROR_BASE_URL` to the committed mirror URL, so the throttled snapshot.debian.org path stops being the silent default. Setting `APT_MIRROR_BASE_URL` overrides the mirror; setting it empty forces the snapshot.debian.org fallback (mirror outage degrades to slow, never to wrong).
- `GET /snap/<T>/<archive>/dists/...` serves index files frozen verbatim at cut time from R2 (404 when the T isn't cut; no read-through for dists). Upstream Debian signatures are intact, so apt verifies with the stock keyring.
- `GET /snap/<T>/<archive>/pool/...` serves from the shared immutable pool cache: R2 hit → immediate (with `Cache-Control: immutable` and Cloudflare edge caching); miss → read through to the live archive, then snapshot.debian.org at T for superseded files, streaming to the client while persisting to R2 in the background. Cache writes are strictly best-effort — the client always gets the fetched bytes; a failed write just means the next request re-fetches. Unsafe paths and malformed timestamps get 400s; files missing everywhere get 404s.
- `Range` requests are honored on R2 hits (apt download resume); cold read-through misses ignore the header and return the full 200 body, which apt handles.
- Anyone can fetch from the mirror (fully public for v1); abuse is watched via Cloudflare's built-in Workers/R2 analytics (`wrangler tail` for live debugging), with rules added later only if needed.
- Operators cut a new T with `uv run apt-mirror cut --timestamp <T>` (idempotent, minutes): the full index set for the configured suites/architectures is frozen from snapshot.debian.org into R2, checksums verified against the signed Release manifests. On success, `cut` rewrites `apps/apt_mirror/current-timestamp` in the local checkout and reminds the operator to commit it.
- `uv run apt-mirror warm` resolves the committed package lists (`apps/apt_mirror/package_lists/*.txt`, all lists by default) against the cut T's Packages indexes for amd64+arm64, fetches missing pool files in parallel directly into R2, and exits nonzero if any listed file is unfetchable on all upstreams. `uv run apt-mirror verify` performs the same check read-only. Both default T to the committed `current-timestamp`.
- The release runbook (release.md step 0) becomes: cut → warm → commit `current-timestamp` → mirror the same T into dwt's `.mngr/apt-snapshot-timestamp` (the runbook requires the two files to match at T-bump time). No connector URL, no admin key.
- The connector loses the four mirror routes and goes back to a genuinely self-contained `app.py` (no monorepo imports, no `boto3`/`imbue-common`/`loguru` in its image); its deploys stop being broken by the mirror code. Nothing consumed the connector-hosted routes yet, so nothing else changes behavior.
- A release test (not per-PR CI) proves the real path end to end: a trixie container runs `apt-get update && apt-get install` against the live mirror at the committed T. Worker unit tests (workerd runtime, mocked upstream fetch) and the existing CLI/service unit tests run in normal CI.
- Bring-up is operator-executed from a committed runbook in the new project's README: create the R2 bucket + scoped R2 keys + Workers-deploy token in the production Cloudflare account, push the Vault entry, `just deploy-apt-mirror`, attach `apt.imbuepackages.com`, cut the already-committed T (`20260725T000000Z`), warm, verify from a scratch trixie container — and only then land the dwt default-URL change (which stays on this branch pair).

## Changes

- New `apps/apt_mirror/` project (README with bring-up runbook + operations doc, changelog dir, `test_ratchets.py`, `current-timestamp`, `package_lists/`):
  - `worker/`: a pnpm + TypeScript wrangler project (committed lockfile, `apt-mirror` Worker name, `apt-mirror` R2 binding, `apt.imbuepackages.com` custom domain) implementing the two serve routes with path validation, read-through, edge caching, Range-on-hit, and bounded upstream 5xx retries; unit-tested with `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers`.
  - A Python package providing the `apt-mirror` console script (`cut` / `warm` / `verify`), ported from the existing `apt_mirror.py` service, storage, fetcher, and parsing code — now free to use `imbue_common` and normal monorepo style, with warm's serial time-budget walk replaced by parallel fetching of the resolved package-list closure and the HTTP request/response models reshaped into CLI results.
  - The first package list, hand-derived from dwt's `setup_system.sh` + `env.d` installs; more lists later (common packages, one-time backfill).
- Remove the mirror from `remote_service_connector`: the four routes and their imports in `app.py`, `apt_mirror.py` and its tests (they move), the `boto3` pyproject dependency, and the `boto3`/`imbue-common`/`loguru` image installs added for it.
- Credentials: repurpose `.minds/template/apt-mirror.sh` into the schema for one Vault entry at `secrets/minds/production/apt-mirror` holding the CLI's R2 access keys plus a dedicated Workers-deploy Cloudflare token (kept separate from the connector's token so registry access is independently auditable).
- Deployment: a manual `just deploy-apt-mirror` recipe wrapping `wrangler deploy` with the token from Vault/env; no CI deploys. A CI job runs the worker's vitest suite when `apps/apt_mirror/worker/` changes.
- dwt (in `.external_worktrees/default-workspace-template`, same branch): `write_apt_sources.sh` defaults to `https://apt.imbuepackages.com`, override/empty semantics preserved; lands only after bring-up verification.
- Docs: rewrite release.md step 0 for the CLI flow and the current-timestamp/dwt matching rule; update the connector README; note the ops ownership (production Cloudflare account, keep-forever bucket) in the new README.
- Tests: worker vitest unit tests; ported Python unit tests for parsing/cut/warm/verify against the existing mock storage/fetcher; a release test driving a real trixie container against the live mirror; connector tests updated for the route removal.
